sentences.text: Protoplotus was an extinct genus of small waterbirds that inhabited freshwater rift lakes in Indonesia during the early to mid-Cenozoic, likely in the Eocene.
The single known species, P. beauforti, is known from a largely complete and well-preserved skeleton found in the Sangkarewang Formation.
Scientists first described this genus in 1931 by Lambrecht.

Although Protoplotus resembled modern cormorants and darters in appearance and lifestyle, recent studies show it is distinct from both groups. It now belongs to its own family, Protoplotidae, which is related to both cormorants and darters.
These birds lived from the Danian to the Priabonian stages, spanning between 66 and 33.9 million years ago.
